## Purpose and entry points
OpenTelemetry .NET Contrib is a multi-package .NET repository for OpenTelemetry libraries outside the core .NET SDK scope: instrumentations, exporters, resource detectors, samplers, enrichment, control-plane support, and storage. It produces independently versioned/maturity-tiered NuGet components rather than one deployable application. Build entry points are `opentelemetry-dotnet-contrib.slnx` and `opentelemetry-dotnet-contrib.proj`; consumer-facing entry points are package-specific OpenTelemetry builder extensions, e.g. `src/OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore/AspNetCoreInstrumentationTracerProviderBuilderExtensions.cs` and `src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InfluxDB/InfluxDBExporterExtensions.cs`.

## Instrumentation adapters
Instrumentation packages attach to application/library lifecycle mechanisms—DiagnosticSource listeners, middleware, interceptors, SDK pipelines, or client wrappers—to create traces and metrics with semantic attributes. Major representative implementations include HTTP client instrumentation at `src/OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http/Implementation/HttpHandlerDiagnosticListener.cs`, ASP.NET Core incoming-request instrumentation at `src/OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore/Implementation/HttpInListener.cs`, and database instrumentation at `src/OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.SqlClient/Implementation/SqlClientDiagnosticListener.cs`. Other packages follow this same integration boundary for AWS, Kafka, gRPC, EF Core, Redis, WCF, runtime/process metrics, and schedulers.

## Shared telemetry normalization
`src/Shared` supplies cross-package implementation primitives for subscribing to diagnostics, creating Activities/Meters, propagating context, processing request/database metadata, and applying conventions. Key boundaries are `src/Shared/DiagnosticSourceSubscriber.cs`, `src/Shared/ActivityInstrumentationHelper.cs`, and `src/Shared/SqlProcessor.cs`. `src/OpenTelemetry.SemanticConventions` publishes generated, strongly named attribute constants—such as `src/OpenTelemetry.SemanticConventions/Attributes/HttpAttributes.cs`—separating specification vocabulary from individual instrumentation behavior.

## Pipeline extensions, enrichment, and dynamic policy
General extensions augment OpenTelemetry SDK pipelines: samplers and processors in `src/OpenTelemetry.Extensions/TracerProviderBuilderExtensions.cs`, trace enrichment in `src/OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Enrichment/Internal/TraceEnrichmentProcessor.cs`, and framework-specific enrichment registration in `src/OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Enrichment.AspNetCore/AspNetCoreTraceEnrichmentProviderBuilderExtensions.cs`. Dynamic Control is a separate policy domain: it parses provider data into telemetry policies, stores versioned snapshots, and notifies subscribers through `src/OpenTelemetry.DynamicControl/Internal/Providers/PolicyReader.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.DynamicControl/Internal/Store/PolicyStore.cs`, and `src/OpenTelemetry.DynamicControl/Internal/Store/PolicyChangeNotifier.cs`.

## Export and persistence boundaries
Exporters transform OpenTelemetry records into destination-specific schemas and transports. Geneva supports logs, traces, and metrics with platform-native transports (`src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Geneva/GenevaTraceExporter.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Geneva/Internal/Transports/EtwDataTransport.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.Geneva/Internal/Transports/UnixDomainSocketDataTransport.cs`). OneCollector serializes logs to Common Schema JSON and posts over HTTP (`src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OneCollector/Internal/Serialization/LogRecordCommonSchemaJsonSerializer.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OneCollector/Internal/Transports/HttpJsonPostTransport.cs`). InfluxDB exports metrics through Telegraf/Prometheus writers (`src/OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InfluxDB/InfluxDBMetricsExporter.cs`). Persistent storage is abstracted from filesystem implementation via `src/OpenTelemetry.PersistentStorage.Abstractions/PersistentBlobProvider.cs` and `src/OpenTelemetry.PersistentStorage.FileSystem/FileBlobProvider.cs`.

## Runtime, cloud, and control-plane integrations
Resource packages detect deployment identity from host, process, container, and cloud metadata: `src/OpenTelemetry.Resources.AWS/AWSEC2Detector.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.Resources.Azure/AzureVMResourceDetector.cs`, and `src/OpenTelemetry.Resources.Container/ContainerDetector.cs`. AWS-specific tracing includes X-Ray propagation and remote sampling (`src/OpenTelemetry.Extensions.AWS/Trace/AWSXRayPropagator.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.Sampler.AWS/AWSXRayRemoteSampler.cs`), requiring AWS service endpoints/metadata where configured. The OpAmp client communicates with a remote OpenTelemetry control plane using HTTP or WebSocket transports, frames protocol messages, and manages heartbeat/remote configuration: `src/OpenTelemetry.OpAmp.Client/OpAmpClient.cs`, `src/OpenTelemetry.OpAmp.Client/Internal/OpAmpPipe.cs`, and `src/OpenTelemetry.OpAmp.Client/Internal/Transport/WebSocket/WsTransport.cs`.

## Runtime and delivery
The codebase targets the .NET ecosystem across modern .NET and selected legacy framework integrations (notably ASP.NET, WCF, and remoting). Central package/build policy resides in `Directory.Build.props` and `Directory.Packages.props`. CI is GitHub Actions, with package publication in `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`; releases publish NuGet packages, with nightly packages referenced through MyGet.
